nodes.label: Bottom-Up Documentation
nodes.rationale: Leaf modules are documented first so parent overviews can be synthesized from completed child Markdown.

nodes.label: Cache-First Processing
nodes.rationale: A cache hit avoids cloning, dependency analysis, and LLM work for repeated repository requests.

nodes.label: Receiver-First Call Resolution
nodes.rationale: Inspecting receivers allows member calls to resolve against this, super, known classes, inferred instances, or typed variables before falling back to bare names.

nodes.label: MCP Stdio Payload Avoidance
nodes.rationale: Large artifacts are stored in per-session workspaces so stdio carries only a session ID and small control messages.

nodes.label: Shared Analysis-to-Documentation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: CLI, web, and MCP entry points converge on dependency analysis, module clustering, LLM generation, and validated output.

nodes.label: Shallow Type Inference
nodes.rationale: Single-assignment receiver tracking resolves common attribute calls without attempting full flow-sensitive analysis.

nodes.label: Thin Front-Ends
nodes.rationale: Each interface owns input/output concerns while delegating documentation work to the shared backend pipeline.

nodes.label: Artifact-Dependent Build Behavior
nodes.rationale: Build, configuration, packaging, deployment, and test artifacts must be read when behavior depends on how the system is built or operated.

nodes.label: Essential Artifact Components
nodes.rationale: Artifact components are essential and must be grouped or attached rather than dropped.

nodes.label: Minimal Documentation Edits
nodes.rationale: Only stale items should change; prose that remains true should be preserved word for word.

nodes.label: Architectural Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Subsystems should reflect shared architectural roles rather than directory names, and every module should belong to exactly one subsystem.

nodes.label: Component-Level Incremental Updater
nodes.rationale: The updater edits only affected pages and can fall back to a full build when a change is too large.

nodes.label: Surgical Documentation Edits
nodes.rationale: Only pages in the write set may be edited, while still-true sentences are kept unchanged.

nodes.label: Atomic Skill Installation
nodes.rationale: The install target stages and validates a package before replacing the destination, preserving an existing installation when validation fails.

nodes.norm_label: dependency graph diff and module-tree repair

nodes.label: Artifact dependency graph
nodes.rationale: CodeWiki 2.0 makes build, deployment, and configuration files first-class graph nodes because the 1.x pipeline dropped them before node creation.

nodes.label: Component-level incremental updates
nodes.rationale: The updater uses components as the change unit and leaf modules as the work unit so comment-only changes do not churn downstream documentation.

nodes.label: MCP IDE-driven mode
nodes.rationale: The IDE agent supplies reasoning while CodeWiki supplies the analysis toolchain, avoiding a second LLM configuration.
